papers.title: User Preference-aware Fake News Detection
papers.venue: Proceedings of the 44th International ACM SIGIR Conference on Research and Development in Information Retrieval
papers.method: UPFD: news root node plus user nodes (features from users' historical tweets) in a retweet tree; one GNN layer, readout, concatenation with the news embedding
papers.findings: Full text (TeX source): Table 2 already includes news-only baselines (BERT+MLP 71.04 / 85.76 acc, word2vec+MLP 76.47 / 84.61 on POL / GOS) against UPFD 84.62 / 97.23. Section 3.3 ablation '-EXO' removes all edges: accuracy 85.61 vs 81.63 on PolitiFact and 95.47 vs 93.92 on the second dataset (the text labels both sentences 'Politifact'). Five runs, t-test, 20/10/70 split.
papers.limitations: No standard deviations reported. The ablation's full model (GCNFN, word2vec, no news concatenation) reports 85.61, above the 80.54 for GCNFN with word2vec in Table 3; the difference is not explained.

papers.title: The Impact of Data Characteristics on GNN Evaluation for Detecting Fake News
papers.method: Five GNNs (GCN, GAT, GraphSAGE, GCNFN, GNNCL) against an MLP that mean-pools all node features; feature shuffling, edge rewiring and synthetic ego-graphs
papers.datasets: UPFD PolitiFact and GossipCop, BERT (768-d) features only
papers.findings: Full text (TeX source): stratified 10-fold CV, mean validation accuracy with 95% CI. Table 2: GossipCop GCNFN 96.1 +/- 1.6 vs MLP 90.8 +/- 3.0; PolitiFact GCNFN 82.7 +/- 5.5 vs MLP 74.3 +/- 7.4. Edge rewiring leaves accuracy above 90% on GossipCop; feature shuffling collapses GAT/GraphSAGE to chance while GCN and GNNCL keep about 80% on GossipCop, which the authors attribute to graph size or density. Over 75% of nodes are one hop from the root.
papers.limitations: Preprint, no code found (author portfolio lists it as a preprint). Text and table disagree: MLP on GossipCop 93.87% in text vs 90.8% in Table 2; MLP on PolitiFact 80.93% vs 74.3%; GAT on GossipCop 95.26% vs 91.5%. Reports validation accuracy only (no held-out test). The MLP pools user nodes too, so it does not separate news content from user features.

papers.title: Nothing Stands Alone: Relational Fake News Detection with Hypergraph Neural Networks
papers.method: HGFND: hypergraph neural network over news items, with hyperedges for shared users, shared time windows and shared entities; transductive node classification
papers.datasets: UPFD PolitiFact and GossipCop (news and user information from the UPFD release)
papers.findings: Full text (TeX source): user hyperedges connect news items that share a Twitter user ID (2,953 such users in PolitiFact, 15,646 in GossipCop). With user hyperedges alone the model reaches 87.23 +/- 2.32 (PolitiFact) and 97.29 +/- 0.16 (GossipCop) accuracy; all three hyperedge types give 91.13 / 97.46. Baselines trained with 10 seeds, model chosen on validation. The authors conclude that users play a key role in detecting fake news.
papers.limitations: Treats shared users as intended signal in a transductive setting and states there is no label leakage because test labels are hidden; does not evaluate on unseen users

sections.summary: No-go for the proposal as written: the graph-vs-no-graph comparison on UPFD is already published [@karn2025structure; @dou2021upfd]. The continuation measured on the official split files that a model-free vote over users seen in training reaches 86.0% on PolitiFact and 90.3% on GossipCop, and that repeat users carry identical feature vectors, so every per-graph model can use the shortcut. That shared users predict labels is itself already published [@jeong2022hgfnd]; what appears open is treating it as a confound of per-graph benchmark results. Conditional go for that narrower question, scoped to PolitiFact for controlled experiments.

recommendation.text: Drop the original proposal (no-go) and the stand-alone replication of Karn and Jensen (no-go).

Conditional go for the recurring-user question as a 4-6 week benchmark-validity study. Its first deliverable needs no training: the overlap measurements in this report, written up with the code. Model runs on masked PolitiFact follow only if the three conditions are met.
If the unread chapters turn out to cover it, or a methods-focused project is preferred, switch to the aspect-based sentiment candidate from the opportunity report.

opportunities.title: As proposed: multi-seed graph vs no-graph re-evaluation of UPFD
opportunities.revision_note: Reading the full texts showed the experiment has been done three times: the UPFD paper itself reports news-only baselines and an edge-removal ablation [@dou2021upfd]; Karn and Jensen benchmark five GNNs against a same-feature MLP with 10-fold CIs, edge rewiring and feature shuffling on both UPFD datasets [@karn2025structure]; and DAWN compares a BERT content-only model with GNNs under temporal splits [@kim2025dawn]. A further multi-seed rerun would mainly confirm Karn and Jensen. The audit also found the comparison as designed cannot isolate graph structure (see the revised question).
opportunities.research_question: On UPFD PolitiFact and GossipCop, how much do GNNs over user-engagement graphs add beyond a classifier on news features alone, under 10+ seeds and repeated splits?
opportunities.motivation: Originally proposed as the top-ranked idea of the NLP+GNN opportunity report.

closest_existing_work.how_it_differs: Same comparison (GNNs vs an MLP on identical features, edge rewiring, feature shuffling, CIs) on the same datasets; differs only in reporting validation accuracy and using BERT features only.
News-only MLP baselines and an edge-removal ablation (-EXO), five runs with t-tests.
Content-only BERT vs GNNs under temporal splits on raw FakeNewsNet.

gap_evidence.text: UPFD Table 2 reports news-only baselines (BERT+MLP 71.04% / 85.76%) against UPFD (84.62% / 97.23%) on PolitiFact / GossipCop; the -EXO ablation removes all edges (85.61% vs 81.63% on PolitiFact)
An MLP on the same BERT node features reaches 90.8% +/- 3.0 vs 96.1% +/- 1.6 for GCNFN on GossipCop and 74.3% +/- 7.4 vs 82.7% +/- 5.5 on PolitiFact; edge rewiring leaves GossipCop accuracy above 90%
Under temporal splits a BERT content-only model reaches 84.2% on PolitiFact against 86.4% for GCN (5-run averages, no SD)

novelty.uncertainty: Rejected because the full texts of three papers describe the experiment. The tool's challenge searches returned 'no close match' both times and missed Karn and Jensen, which was found by web search; tool signals for this topic are unreliable.

opportunities.title: Revised (twice): do per-graph UPFD results reflect recurring users rather than content or structure?
opportunities.revision_note: First revision: the graph-vs-no-graph question is answered [@karn2025structure; @dou2021upfd]. Second revision (this continuation): full-text reading of [@jeong2022hgfnd] showed that the predictive power of users shared between news items is already published, as a deliberate transductive signal. What remains open in the sources read is the evaluation question: how much of the accuracy reported for per-graph models on the official UPFD split, and of conclusions such as 'structure adds little', comes from recurring users that the models can recognise through identical feature vectors.
opportunities.research_question: On the official UPFD split, how much of the accuracy of per-graph GNNs and of same-feature MLPs is explained by test users seen in training, and do published conclusions about news content versus propagation structure hold when that shortcut is controlled (PolitiFact: masking seen users; GossipCop: descriptive only)?
opportunities.motivation: Published comparisons on UPFD attribute performance to news content, user preferences or propagation structure [@dou2021upfd; @karn2025structure]. Every model that pools user-node features, including Karn and Jensen's MLP, can also exploit recurring users, and DAWN observes that users tend to engage with only one class [@kim2025dawn]. A review of fake news studies argues reported accuracies are shaped by evaluation design and possible leakage [@tuan2026review].

closest_existing_work.how_it_differs: Uses shared users as a feature (user hyperedges) and reports their predictive power; does not treat them as a confound of per-graph benchmark results or evaluate on unseen users.
Isolates edges and features with rewiring and shuffling; keeps user nodes and random stratified folds in every condition, so the user shortcut is present throughout.
Temporal split on raw FakeNewsNet; notes users' label consistency but does not measure user overlap between splits.
Defines the benchmark and split; no overlap analysis.
Not read; title and a search summary suggest structural analysis, not split leakage.
Not read; title suggests a hypergraph model on UPFD, possibly with user hyperedges.

gap_evidence.text: Official split files (PyG/UPFD train_idx/test_idx; 62 PolitiFact and 1092 GossipCop training graphs): a vote over the training labels of a test graph's users, with no model, text or edges, reaches 86.0% on PolitiFact and 90.2% on GossipCop (majority class 48.9% and 49.9%). 79.6% and 98.8% of test graphs share a user with training.

The shortcut is visible to any model through its inputs: 94.3% (spaCy history features) and 94.7% (profile features) of PolitiFact repeat users, and 86.4% of GossipCop repeat users (profile features), carry an identical feature vector in every graph they appear in. Using the feature vector itself as the identity gives the same vote accuracy (86.0% PolitiFact, 90.8% GossipCop). BERT features were not downloaded and not checked.

Published accuracies on the same data: UPFD 84.62 (PolitiFact) and 97.23 (GossipCop), its news-only MLPs 71.04-76.47 and 84.61-85.76; the same-feature MLP of Karn and Jensen 74.3 and 90.8; HGFND with user hyperedges only 87.23 and 97.29. The model-free user vote is at or above several of these.

That shared users predict veracity is already published: HGFND builds one hyperedge per user shared between news items (2,953 PolitiFact, 15,646 GossipCop, the same counts measured here) and reaches 87.23 / 97.29 accuracy from them alone. It treats this as a legitimate transductive signal, not as a confound of per-graph evaluations.
No source read in full (UPFD, Karn and Jensen, DAWN, HGFND, Xu, Maurya) reports train/test user overlap for per-graph models or evaluates on unseen users.

opportunities.contribution: A short benchmark-validity study: the identity shortcut quantified on the official split, its availability through feature vectors, and whether per-graph models and the 'structure adds little' conclusion change when it is controlled on PolitiFact. Either outcome is reportable; the scope suits a workshop or reproducibility track.

novelty.uncertainty: The observation that users predict labels is published [@jeong2022hgfnd]; only its use as an evaluation confound appears open in the papers read. Three UPFD-related chapters could not be read, Semantic Scholar was rate-limited, and user-disjoint evaluation is common in neighbouring areas under other names (cold-start, inductive users).

feasibility.text: A strict user-disjoint split is infeasible on both datasets: shared users link 93.0% of PolitiFact and 99.6% of GossipCop graphs into one component; even ignoring users in 3+ graphs the largest component holds 85.4% and 54.6%.

Masking test-graph users seen in training is a small change on PolitiFact (8.9% of test user nodes removed; median users per test graph 91 -> 78; 2 graphs emptied) but a large distribution shift on GossipCop (71.6% removed; median 48.0 -> 6.0; 359 graphs emptied).
PolitiFact has 221 official test graphs, so a 95% interval on accuracy is roughly +/- 5-6 points; only large differences between conditions will be detectable.
All checks ran on CPU from about 60 MB of index, label and feature files; models would also be CPU-scale.

evidence.text: Official split files (PyG/UPFD train_idx/test_idx; 62 PolitiFact and 1092 GossipCop training graphs): a vote over the training labels of a test graph's users, with no model, text or edges, reaches 86.0% on PolitiFact and 90.2% on GossipCop (majority class 48.9% and 49.9%). 79.6% and 98.8% of test graphs share a user with training.

methodological_risks.mitigation: Mask seen users in PolitiFact test graphs; report the user vote as a baseline everywhere.

evidence.text: No published UPFD comparison includes a user-identity vote or a graph-size rule; the size rule reaches 74.9% on GossipCop's official test split (fails on PolitiFact: 48.4%).

methodological_risks.mitigation: Include user vote, size rule, root-only MLP and same-feature MLP as baselines.

evidence.text: The official GNN-FakeNews script draws a random split instead of the fixed split files used by PyG, selects no model on validation, and differs from the paper on pooling and weight decay.

methodological_risks.mitigation: Use the fixed split files plus repeated random splits; select on validation.

evidence.text: The official evaluation helper averages macro-F1 over batches.

methodological_risks.mitigation: Compute metrics on the whole test set.

evidence.text: 221 PolitiFact test graphs and 62 training graphs; published comparisons use 5 runs.

methodological_risks.mitigation: 10+ seeds and repeated splits with paired comparisons; report intervals.

evidence.text: Masking test-graph users seen in training is a small change on PolitiFact (8.9% of test user nodes removed; median users per test graph 91 -> 78; 2 graphs emptied) but a large distribution shift on GossipCop (71.6% removed; median 48.0 -> 6.0; 359 graphs emptied).

methodological_risks.mitigation: Make causal claims only for PolitiFact; GossipCop analysed descriptively.

evidence.text: graph_labels match FakeNewsNet's fake/real lists for 313 of 314 PolitiFact and all 5,464 GossipCop graphs (one PolitiFact mismatch unexplained).

methodological_risks.evidence: User features come from historical tweets crawled after the news; their timing was not examined.

decision.rationale: The shortcut is real, large and measured on the official split, and no source read treats it as a confound of per-graph results. But the signal itself is known [@jeong2022hgfnd], the controlled experiment is only clean on PolitiFact (221 test graphs), and three related chapters are unread. Worth doing as a short, scoped benchmark-validity study, not as a full-semester flagship.
conditions: Read [@rai2025hypergraph], [@rai2025attention] and [@bryla2026networks] through the library; if any evaluates per-graph models on unseen users or reports split overlap, reframe as a replication.

Before running models, state the smallest accuracy change on masked PolitiFact that would matter, and check it exceeds the roughly +/- 5-6 point interval from 221 test graphs; if not, keep the study descriptive.
Frame against [@jeong2022hgfnd] (users as a feature) and [@karn2025structure] (structure ablation), not as a discovery that users matter.
unresolved_risks: BERT user features not checked for identity (only spaCy and profile features were).
Whether the user-feature timing leaks post-publication information is unknown.
Reviewers may consider the result implied by HGFND.

opportunities.title: Fallback: independent replication of Karn and Jensen with a held-out test set
opportunities.research_question: Do Karn and Jensen's conclusions (MLP within a few points of GNNs; structure negligible) hold when measured on held-out test data, on the official UPFD split and with all four feature types, and which of their inconsistent reported numbers is correct?
opportunities.motivation: The paper is the closest and most recent evidence on the question, but it is an unreviewed preprint without code whose text and table disagree [@karn2025structure].

closest_existing_work.how_it_differs: The study being replicated; no code is available, so the project is a replication, not a reproduction.

gap_evidence.text: Text and Table 2 disagree (MLP on GossipCop 93.87% vs 90.8%; on PolitiFact 80.93% vs 74.3%; GAT on GossipCop 95.26% vs 91.5%)
Results are mean validation accuracy over 10 folds; no held-out test set is described

opportunities.contribution: A checked set of numbers for a claim others are likely to cite; low novelty.

novelty.uncertainty: A camera-ready version (the acknowledgements mention one) may already correct the inconsistencies; it was not found.

limitations: Novelty of the revised question rests on searches that missed the closest paper on the original question; treat it as unverified until the library check is done.

Graph reconstruction assumes node ids are contiguous per graph with the news node first; this matched the released news list order and the paper's node totals, but was not checked against node_graph_id.npy.
Accounts appearing in thousands of GossipCop graphs were not identified; removing users in 50+ graphs lowered the GossipCop vote accuracy from 91.1% to 83.9%.
Karn and Jensen's text and table disagree; the audit quotes the table where it gives CIs and notes the conflict.
Semantic Scholar was rate-limited throughout; citing works came from OpenAlex and were screened by title only.
No model was trained and no published number was reproduced.
Not read: Bryla et al. 2026, Rai et al. 2025 (two chapters); publisher pages require login.
BERT user features (125 MB PolitiFact, 862 MB GossipCop) were not downloaded; identity was checked on spaCy and profile features (PolitiFact) and profile features (GossipCop).
The user-vote diagnostic shows that identity carries label information; it does not show how much any trained model relies on it. No model was trained.
